title: Pause toggle maps Boot (and any non-Run mode) to Run, not just Run<->Paused
detail: Only Game_Over early-returns; in Boot the ternary maps any non-Run mode to Run, so P/SPACE during the Boot transient force-starts the run instead of toggling pause. The claimed 'Run <-> Paused' gate is not what the code implements.
recommended_fix: Gate on both modes explicitly: if Run -> Paused else if Paused -> Run (ignore Boot), or return early unless mode is Run or Paused.

title: Core test pins boundary hash equality that harness/run.odin explicitly disavows
evidence:
+	for w in u64(11)..=20 {
+		testing.expectf(t, live_hashes[w-1] == live_hashes[9],
+			"pause window must be stable at wall tick %d (%016x != tick-10 %016x)",
...
+	// boundary hash legitimately differs from the last STEPPED tick's hash
+	// (that one included the tick's own events) — the stability contract is
+	// window-internal: the state does not mutate while paused.
...
+1210 df84240b8304c0d5
+1211 d3600eef9503b6d9
detail: Test (a) equates the first paused hash with the last stepped hash; run.odin documents (and pause.t1 shows: 1210 vs 1211 differ) that they legitimately differ when the boundary tick emits events. Passes only because tick 10 is event-free.
recommended_fix: Assert window-internal stability instead: compare paused hashes to live_hashes[10] (the first paused hash), matching run_demo/replay_hashes' pause_base contract.

title: Pause schedule validated for file-order alternation only, not chronological at_ms order
detail: Alternation is validated in file order only, not by at_ms; paused_at/ticks_stepped_by resolve by list order, so mis-ordered directives overlap windows and double-subtract paused ticks — wrong apply_ticks, u64 underflow, or a silently frozen tail.
recommended_fix: After parsing, sort d.pauses by effect tick (or reject non-monotonic at_ms loudly, like double-pause) so the schedule is chronological before lowering/replay.

title: Paused veil and PAUSED label use different window-size sources
detail: The veil sizes from GetScreenWidth/Height but the PAUSED label positions from fixed WIN_W/WIN_H; the main loop explicitly handles window resize, so the label drifts off-center on resized windows.
recommended_fix: Derive label positions from rl.GetScreenWidth()/GetScreenHeight() — the same source the veil rectangle uses.

title: Pause driver logic duplicated between core test and harness virtual clock
evidence:
+record_paused_run :: proc(state: ^Run_State, ticks: u64, pause_from, pause_to: u64, cat: ^Catalogs, allocator := context.allocator) -> [dynamic]u64 {
...
+	sim_tick: u64 = 0
...
+		paused := paused_at(cfg.pauses[:], w, hz)
detail: record_paused_run reimplements the harness virtual-clock driver (sim_tick counting, paused window, command batching) instead of sharing it; the copies already disagree on the stability baseline, so they can drift further.
recommended_fix: Extract one shared pause-driver helper (or drive the core test through the harness contract) so test and harness pin identical semantics.
